semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: 'Music source separation' is a specific application of the broader 'speech separation' domain, focusing on separating musical components instead of just vocal components.

parent_domains.justification: Music source separation falls under the broad category of processing audio signals, specifically separating different audio sources.

The general domain of audio encompasses all research and techniques related to sound, including music source separation.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Music source separation is fundamentally about processing and manipulating the audio signal to separate different components, making 'audio signal processing' the most direct parent domain.

child_domains.justification: Once music source separation is performed, audio classification might be used to categorize the separated components.

closest_child_domain.justification: After performing music source separation, classifying the separated audio parts is a natural next step, making this the closest child domain.

sibling_domains.justification: Both domains deal with extracting useful information from music, although MIR is broader and includes tasks like source separation.
